comments.body:
I would like to work on this, the quickest fix looks like it is to add a guard so that

`lax.cond(pred, lambda: True, lambda: False)` would raise an error if the predicate is varying implying the user needs to write

```
lax.cond(
    pred,
    lambda: lax.pcast(True, "i", to="varying"),
    lambda: lax.pcast(False, "i", to="varying"),
)
```
Which I think makes sense from a parallelism perspective (From a model perspective, we're dealing with one copy of [True, True, True True] or [False False False False] if `pred` is varying and multiple copies of True and False for each shard of `pred` if pred is replicated. The only clean way of not introducing differences between devices when there are not is to explicitly state that beforehand.

I think the label `varying` is a bit confusing in this regard, I feel like it means 'distributed' rather than whether it's varying or not.

The other version is to let do variance propagation where if 

if pred is varying , left_fun is replicated, right_fun is replicated, we get a varying result. (Although gradients through that look iffy)

issue.body:
### Description

## Examples
This issue popped up when dealing with https://github.com/patrick-kidger/equinox/pull/1262. I will explain it with a contrived gradient example below with 2 CPU devices

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from jax import lax
from jax.sharding import Mesh, PartitionSpec as P

mesh = Mesh(np.array(jax.devices()), ("i",))

@jax.shard_map(
    mesh=mesh, in_specs=P(), out_specs=P("i"), check_vma=True
)
def f(x):
    return lax.cond(
        lax.axis_index("i") == 0,
        lambda x: 2 * x,
        lambda x: 3 * x,
        x,
    )[None]

print(f(2.))
print(jax.jit(jax.grad(lambda x: f(x).sum()))(2.))
```

The correct expected gradient is 5, but we end up getting 4. 

For a less contrived example where not having that information is a setback, I reproduce my example in the comment here https://github.com/patrick-kidger/equinox/pull/1262

```python
x = [0, 1, 2, 3]   # device 1 has [0, 1] , device 2 has [2, 3], edited
condition = x[0] < 1.5 
pred = lax.cond(condition, lambda: True, lambda: False) # lax.cond loses information that the predicate is varying but the array is actually # device 1 has [True, True], device 2 has [False False]

result = eqx.error_if(x, pred, "negative", on_error="nan") # attempted sharding assumes predicate is not varying i.e distributed, therefore it will try to forego pmax and can only give wrong result without comms
```

## Timeline of relevant issues/PRs
I'll only keep the illustrative ones, that are relevant to changes in behavior/have unexpected behavior (I filtered the list I got from chatgpt)

1. https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/24418 Issue similar to one of my examples, where we get an exception raise because of the lack of replication rules
2. https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/24877 PR adding replication rules for cond
3. https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/commit/76271d638ad94f3df854054640f3b35161ee5be4 Here the relevant code is 

```python
  b0_vma = [o.vma for o in branches[0].out_avals]
  for branch in branches[1:]:
    b_vma = [o.vma for o in branch.out_avals]
    if b0_vma != b_vma:
      raise Exception("The branches of cond produced mismatched varying manual "
                      f"axes. Got {b0_vma} and {b_vma}. Please open an issue "
                      "at https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues, and as a "
                      "temporary workaround pass the check_rep=False argument "
                      "to shard_map")
```

Note that the code only checks the branches of the axes. If the predicate itself is differently satisfied on different processors, it will lead to a varying output. 

The original replicating code was later deleted in https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/27929


## fix
imo if `pred` is varying in cond(pred, true_fun, false_fun) then the output should be varying as well, and should not raise an error

jaxlib: 0.11.2
numpy:  2.2.6
python: 3.12.13 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Mar  5 2026, 16:50:00) [GCC 14.3.0]

issue.body:
An attempt at #40823
Note that I tried doing a minimal fix but I ended up in a rabbit hole no thanks to trying to get the gradient tests to pass

The current version passes tests on my device, and fixes #40823 with the rule that a varying predicate should give a varying output /however/ I'm not comfortable taking it out of a draft for 2 reasons


1. I did use codex and it's a lot of AI generated code to throw at a maintainer at first pass, and I'm not sure I understand it well enough to be responsible for it. By understanding I mean, I spent a full day looking into the internals and quite a bit of the control flow line by line, looked at similar Trace/Tracer components elsewhere, but I do not know whether it could introduce hidden regressions. When I was generating code, I tried to make sure this was the smallest possible change that fixed the issue, passed the tests and did not introduce regressions


2. I'm not sure what the best design decision is, A guard may be a better design, and is much simpler, at the cost of making the user do more work, and I'm not too familiar with any other hidden approaches. I just went with trying to make the output varying if the predicate was varying because it made the most rational sense.


I just decided it's best left out in the open first as a proposal attached to the issue before I spend extra time to polish it and ask for proper review (in case, say a guard is better)
